practiceQuestions.q: Under which Article of the Indian Constitution is the State Public Service Commission (SPSC) established?
practiceQuestions.sol: Article 315 of the Constitution of India provides for the establishment of a Public Service Commission for the Union and a Public Service Commission for each State. Article 312 deals with All-India Services, Article 320 with functions of Public Service Commissions, and Article 324 with the Election Commission.

practiceQuestions.q: Who has the authority to appoint the Chairman and members of a State Public Service Commission?
practiceQuestions.sol: The Chairman and members of an SPSC are appointed by the Governor of the state. However, they can be removed from office only by the President of India.

practiceQuestions.q: What is the normal tenure of office for the Chairman and members of a State Public Service Commission?
opts: 5 years or 60 years of age, whichever is earlier
6 years or 62 years of age, whichever is earlier
6 years or 65 years of age, whichever is earlier
5 years or 65 years of age, whichever is earlier
practiceQuestions.sol: The Chairman and members of an SPSC hold office for a term of 6 years or until they attain the age of 62 years, whichever is earlier. (Note: For UPSC, the age limit is 65 years).

practiceQuestions.q: To whom does the Chairman of a State Public Service Commission submit their annual resignation or report?
opts: Speaker of the State Legislative Assembly
practiceQuestions.sol: Although appointed by the Governor, the Chairman and members of an SPSC can resign at any time by addressing their resignation letter to the President of India.

practiceQuestions.q: Who has the power to determine the number of members and their conditions of service in a State Public Service Commission?
practiceQuestions.sol: The Constitution does not specify the strength of the SPSC but has left the matter to the discretion of the Governor. Thus, the Governor determines the composition and conditions of service of the SPSC members.

practiceQuestions.q: What constitutional requirement is specified regarding the composition of members in a State Public Service Commission?
opts: All members must be judicial experts
At least 50% members must belong to the medical field
No specific qualifications are prescribed except that one-half of the members should have held office under the government
At least one-third of the members must be women
practiceQuestions.sol: The Constitution does not prescribe the qualifications of the commission members except that one-half of the members of the commission should be persons who have held office for at least ten years either under the Government of India or under the government of a state.

practiceQuestions.q: To whom does the State Public Service Commission present its annual performance report?
practiceQuestions.sol: The SPSC presents an annual report on its performance to the Governor of the state. The Governor then places this report before both houses of the state legislature, along with a memorandum.

practiceQuestions.q: Can the jurisdiction of a State Public Service Commission be extended?
opts: Yes, by an act of the State Legislature
Yes, by an ordinance issued by the Governor alone
No, it is rigidly fixed by the Constitution
Yes, by a notification issued by the President of India
practiceQuestions.sol: The jurisdiction of an SPSC can be extended by an act passed by the State Legislature. It can place the personnel matters of any local authority, corporate body, or public institution within the jurisdiction of the SPSC.

practiceQuestions.q: Which Articles of the Indian Constitution (Part XIV) deal with the Public Service Commissions for the Union and the States?
practiceQuestions.sol: Articles 315 to 323 in Part XIV of the Indian Constitution contain elaborate provisions regarding the composition, appointment, removal, powers, and functions of the UPSC and SPSCs.

practiceQuestions.q: What is the status of the expenses of a State Public Service Commission?
opts: Charged upon the Consolidated Fund of India
Charged upon the Consolidated Fund of the State
Subject to annual vote of the State Legislature
Funded directly by the Union Ministry of Finance
practiceQuestions.sol: The expenses of the SPSC, including any salaries, allowances, and pensions payable to or in respect of the members or staff of the Commission, are charged upon the Consolidated Fund of the State and are non-votable by the legislature.

practiceQuestions.q: Why are the Chairman and members of a State Public Service Commission barred from further employment under the Government of India or any State Government after their retirement?
opts: To reduce government expenditure on pensions
To ensure absolute neutrality, impartiality, and independence from political or executive influence
To provide opportunities for younger bureaucrats
To comply with international labor standards
practiceQuestions.sol: To ensure absolute independence and prevent any temptation of post-retirement sinecures offered by the executive, the Constitution bars the SPSC Chairman from further employment under the government, though an SPSC member can be appointed as Chairman of UPSC or SPSC.

practiceQuestions.q: Which body holds the constitutional power to remove a member or Chairman of a State Public Service Commission from office?
opts: Governor of the State on the advice of the State Cabinet
President of India on the report of the Supreme Court
State Legislative Assembly by a two-thirds majority
High Court of the respective state
practiceQuestions.sol: Although appointed by the Governor, the Chairman or members of an SPSC can be removed only by the President (on grounds of misbehavior after Supreme Court inquiry, insolvency, infirmity, or taking paid employment elsewhere), thereby ensuring high institutional independence.

practiceQuestions.q: What is the nature of the functions performed by a State Public Service Commission according to the Indian Constitution?
opts: Mandatory and binding in all personnel administration decisions
Advisory in nature, and the government can override them with valid justification
Judicial and quasi-judicial with final binding verdicts
Legislative advisory requiring ratification by the Parliament
practiceQuestions.sol: The recommendations of the SPSC are advisory in nature and not binding on the government. The government can depart from the advice, though it may have to explain the reasons to the state legislature if required.

practiceQuestions.q: How does a Joint State Public Service Commission (JSPSC) differ from an SPSC in terms of its creation?
opts: JSPSC is created directly by an amendment to the Constitution under Article 368.
JSPSC is created by an act of Parliament upon a request by the state legislatures concerned.
JSPSC is created by executive order of the President.
JSPSC is created by a joint resolution of the Governors of the respective states.
practiceQuestions.sol: Unlike an SPSC which is created by Article 315 of the Constitution itself, a Joint State Public Service Commission (JSPSC) for two or more states can be created by an Act of Parliament on a request made by the state legislatures concerned.

practiceQuestions.q: Who appoints the Chairman and members of a Joint State Public Service Commission (JSPSC)?
opts: Governors of the respective states jointly
Union Minister of Personnel, Public Grievances and Pensions
Chief Ministers of the participating states by consensus
practiceQuestions.sol: A crucial constitutional distinction is that while members and Chairman of an SPSC are appointed by the Governor, the Chairman and members of a *Joint* State Public Service Commission (JSPSC) are appointed by the President of India.

practiceQuestions.q: Can the state government exclude certain posts or appointments from the purview of the State Public Service Commission?
opts: No, all state appointments must compulsorily go through the SPSC.
Yes, the Governor can make regulations specifying the matters in which, down to certain limits, the SPSC need not be consulted.
Yes, but only through a constitutional amendment passed by the state legislature.
No, only the Union Public Service Commission can exempt posts.
practiceQuestions.sol: The Constitution empowers the Governor to exclude certain posts, matters, or classes of appointments from the consultation purview of the SPSC. However, such regulations must be laid before the state legislature for at least 14 days.

practiceQuestions.q: To whom does a Joint State Public Service Commission submit its annual report?
opts: The Governors of each of the respective participating states
practiceQuestions.sol: A JSPSC presents its annual report on its performance to each of the Governors of the participating states. Each Governor then places the report before the respective state legislature.

practiceQuestions.q: What is the primary role of an SPSC regarding disciplinary matters of civil servants?
opts: To act as a final appellate tribunal punishing corrupt officers
To be consulted on all disciplinary matters affecting a civil servant serving under the state government
To frame the criminal code applicable to state employees
To directly dismiss or suspend officers accused of dereliction of duty
practiceQuestions.sol: The SPSC must be consulted on all disciplinary matters relating to civil services under a state, such as memorial or petitions relating to disciplinary actions, withholding of increments, or dismissal. However, its advice remains advisory.

practiceQuestions.q: Why does the Constitution not provide for a single unified Public Service Commission for both the Centre and the States?
opts: Due to financial constraints of the Central Government
To uphold the federal structure of the Indian polity by giving states autonomy in personnel recruitment
Because state civil services require lower standards of recruitment
To prevent the Union Public Service Commission from becoming overburdened with administrative work
practiceQuestions.sol: India has a federal framework under the Constitution, which envisages a dual polity. Allowing separate SPSCs for states ensures administrative autonomy and meets the specific regional governance and language requirements of the states.

practiceQuestions.q: Can the Governor extend the functions of the SPSC to advise on matters relating to local bodies or public sector undertakings?
opts: Yes, with the prior approval of the President of India
Yes, if an Act passed by the State Legislature enables such extension
No, the Constitution strictly limits SPSC to state civil services alone
Yes, through an executive resolution of the state cabinet
practiceQuestions.sol: The Legislature of a state can provide for the exercise of additional functions by the SPSC in respect of the services of any local authority, public sector undertaking, or other corporate body constituted by law.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the State Public Service Commission (SPSC):
1. The Chairman and members of an SPSC are appointed by the Governor of the state.
2. They hold office for a term of six years or until they attain the age of 65 years, whichever is earlier.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is correct: The Chairman and members of an SPSC are appointed by the Governor. Statement 2 is incorrect because the retirement age for SPSC members is 62 years (not 65 years, which applies to the UPSC).

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the removal of members of a State Public Service Commission:
1. The Governor of the state can remove an SPSC member for misbehavior if the Supreme Court upholds the inquiry.
2. An SPSC member can be removed by the President if they are adjudged an insolvent.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is incorrect because SPSC members are removed by the President of India, not the Governor, even on grounds of misbehavior after Supreme Court inquiry. Statement 2 is correct: the President can remove a member if they are adjudged an insolvent.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the independence of a State Public Service Commission:
The conditions of service of the Chairman or a member of an SPSC cannot be varied to their disadvantage after their appointment.
2. The entire expenses of the SPSC are subject to the annual vote of the State Legislative Assembly.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is correct: their conditions of service cannot be varied to their disadvantage after appointment. Statement 2 is incorrect because the expenses are *charged* upon the Consolidated Fund of the State, meaning they are non-votable by the legislature.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the eligibility for re-appointment of SPSC members:
1. A member of an SPSC is eligible for appointment as the Chairman of UPSC.
2. The Chairman of an SPSC is eligible for further employment under the Government of India.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is correct: an SPSC member can be appointed as Chairman/member of UPSC or Chairman of that or any other SPSC. Statement 2 is incorrect because the Chairman of an SPSC is *not* eligible for any further employment under the Government of India or a State Government.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the Joint State Public Service Commission (JSPSC):
1. A JSPSC can be created by an agreement between two or more states without the intervention of Parliament.
2. The Chairman and members of a JSPSC are appointed by the President of India.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is incorrect because a JSPSC cannot be created by a mere executive agreement between states; it requires an Act of Parliament upon a request made by the state legislatures. Statement 2 is correct: their appointment is made by the President.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the functions of the State Public Service Commission:
1. It conducts examinations for appointments to the services of the state.
2. It is consulted on all matters relating to methods of recruitment to civil services and posts.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Both statements are correct. Article 320 outlines the functions of Public Service Commissions, which include conducting exams for state appointments and being consulted on recruitment methods, principles for promotions/transfers, and disciplinary matters.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the advisory nature of SPSC recommendations:
1. The recommendations made by the SPSC are binding on the state government.
2. If the state government rejects the advice of the SPSC, it is not required to provide any explanation to anyone.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Both statements are incorrect. Statement 1 is wrong because SPSC recommendations are purely advisory. Statement 2 is wrong because whenever the government departs from SPSC advice, it generally needs to present a memorandum explaining the reasons before the state legislature.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the composition and qualifications of SPSC members:
1. The Constitution clearly specifies the exact number of members to be appointed in every State Public Service Commission.
2. One-half of the members of the SPSC must have held office under the Central or State Government for at least ten years.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is incorrect because the Constitution does not specify the strength of the SPSC; it leaves it to the discretion of the Governor. Statement 2 is correct: one-half of the members must have held office for at least 10 years under the government.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the reporting mechanism of an SPSC:
1. The SPSC presents its annual report to the Chief Minister of the state.
2. The Governor places this annual report along with a memorandum before the state legislature.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is incorrect because the SPSC submits its annual report to the *Governor*, not the Chief Minister. Statement 2 is correct: the Governor places the report before the state legislature along with a memorandum explaining cases where SPSC advice was not accepted.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the relationship between UPSC and SPSC:
1. An SPSC can request the Union Public Service Commission (UPSC) to serve all or any of its needs with the approval of the President of India.
2. The UPSC assists states in framing and operating schemes of joint recruitment for any services requiring special qualifications.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Both statements are correct under Article 315(4) and Article 315(3) respectively, which permit the UPSC to serve the needs of a state or assist in joint recruitment upon request with the approval of the President.
